items.item_text: Education/Training: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major coursework in business administration, marketing, education, communications, social sciences, or a related field.

The following describes the education, experience, knowledge, skills and abilities required to enter the job and/or be learned within a short period of time in order to successfully perform the assigned duties.

Education and Experience Guidelines – Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the knowledge and abilities would be:

Experience: Two years of experience in training and development, nonprofit management, continuing education, or community program administration, including one year of administrative or lead supervisory responsibility.
Operations, services, and activities of lifelong learning or enrichment programs for higher education.
Provide program management and strategic direction for community education and lifelong learning programs.
Principles and practices of curriculum planning and development for adults.
Supervise, organize, and review the work of assigned staff involved in the development and administration of community programs, services, and classes.
Methods and techniques of marketing and advertising for community/nonprofit programs.
Select, train, and evaluate staff.
Methods and techniques of public relations.
Develop and recommend program goals, objectives, policies, and procedures; implement approved policies and procedures to ensure the quality and effectiveness of classes and programs.
Principles of supervision, training, and performance evaluation.
Understand the organization and operation of the District and of outside agencies as necessary to assume assigned responsibilities.
Principles and practices of program administration, strategic planning, resource allocation, and program evaluation.
Understand, interpret, and apply general and specific administrative and departmental policies and procedures as well as applicable federal, state, and local policies, laws, and regulations.
Partnership development and collaborative program planning in educational, nonprofit, and community settings.
Prepare clear and concise reports and professional correspondence.
Basic principles and practices of budget preparation and administration.
Participate in the preparation and administration of assigned budgets.
Principles and procedures of recordkeeping.
Assess program staffing and instructional needs and establish processes for recruiting, selecting, and evaluating contracted instructors.
Principles of business letter writing and basic report preparation.
Plan and organize work to meet changing priorities and deadlines.
Modern office procedures, methods, and equipment including computers.
Effectively represent the District to outside individuals and agencies to accomplish the goals and objectives of the unit.
Computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, and statistical databases.
Work cooperatively with other departments, District staff, and outside agencies.
Pertinent federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations.
Respond tactfully, clearly and concisely, and appropriately to inquiries from the public, District staff, or other agencies on sensitive issues in area of responsibility.
Demonstrate an awareness and appreciation of the cultural diversity of the community.
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing.
